$about: The Subo terminology lexicon. ONE file, vendored byte-identical in subo-site/ and subo/,
the way .claude/skills/subo-glossary/ already is: edit one, copy to the other in the same change.
It exists because the markdown skill drifted. The FR poll row went stale across two naming
rounds and nobody noticed, because nothing could check it. This file is checkable:
`npm run check:lexicon` enforces the parts a machine can enforce.
Reasoning lives in docs/authority-roadmap.md (TERMINOLOGY ARCHITECTURE). Rulings referenced
here as T1..T10 are defined there. Do not restate the reasoning in this file; it will drift.
Two vocabularies, joined at one named point per surface.
Problem vocabulary (demand side) = what someone calls their need before they know Subo.
Product vocabulary (supply side) = what Subo actually has.
The rule that decides which gets translated: LOCALIZE WHAT THE PLATFORM OWNS, BRAND WHAT YOU OWN.

poll.$why: poll is Discord's primitive and Discord already localized it. Adopt Discord's word per locale (T2b). Fighting the platform's vocabulary is unwinnable.

convo.$why: Convo is Subo's invention, so it stays invariant in every locale (T3). Capitalized always; lowercase 'convo' is a defect everywhere except identifiers and URL paths.

grammar.$ruling: Convo takes the gender of the local word for CONVERSATION (user, 2026-08-28). It is feminine in every gendered locale we ship, because conversation is: die Konversation, la conversación, la conversation, la conversazione, a conversa, konwersacja, беседа.
grammar.$why: An untranslated brand noun still has to agree with articles and adjectives, and a translator with no ruling picks per string. Deriving the gender from the word Convo is short for keeps every locale internally consistent and matches what the noun means.
grammar.plural: English plural where it reads naturally (DE/ES/FR/NL/PT-BR: Convos); uninflected where the language would decline it (IT/PL/RU: Convo); TR attaches suffixes after an apostrophe.

$about: 'project' is the admin/creator umbrella for one poll or one Convo. Already the public-API
noun (project/projectId, type: convo|poll) and already in 131 English user_messages cells.
AUDIENCE DECIDES THE UMBRELLA (settled 2026-08-26 from the A1b audit):
admin/creator surfaces  -> 'project'
respondent surfaces     -> name the instrument ('poll' / 'Convo'), never 'project'
A member who just answered a question has no concept of a project.
OPEN QUESTION (user, 2026-08-26): reserve 'project' for GROUPS of items instead, e.g. a
tracker grouping survey waves for cross-wave reporting. 'group' is null because that
concept does not ship yet. RECOMMENDATION when it does: give the GROUP a new noun
(tracker / program / series) and leave 'project' on the item. Renaming the item breaks the
public API (project/projectId/type), ~131 strings, the whole web UI and the docs, to free
one word; naming the new concept costs nothing because nothing uses it yet.
Note for anyone reading the code: internally every item is a 'survey' (survey_id,
serverSurvey, SurveyService). That is the code layer and is deliberately NOT user-facing
vocabulary. See T8: code strings are not proof of the live product noun.
Discord's own localized word for its native poll feature, per locale. This is the T2b
reference: a locale's poll word IS Discord's poll word, no exceptions. Evidence standard
T9: a door word ships only if it comes from Discord's localized UI or from search data.
Source: user-supplied from Discord's UI, 2026-08-26.
What the live app actually calls a poll, per locale, from the user_messages export
(user_messages_all_2026-08-18.xlsx). Two surfaces because they can and do disagree.
check:lexicon compares these against discord.pollWord to enforce T2b. This comparison is
the thing nothing in either repo could do before this file existed.
Refresh with `!test user_messages` in Discord, which DMs the xlsx.

$about: One row per shipping locale. `status` says how far the row has been taken:
active            — instruments, a bridge sentence, doors with evidence, and a working deny list.
seeded            — the same, but the doors have no owning URL yet because the pages do not exist.
instruments-only  — instruments and an empty deny list, nothing else. A7a. Recording what a locale
SAYS, which moves nothing a user reads. `doors` and `bridge` are OMITTED, not
empty: both need per-locale search evidence (T9) and that is A7b.
`instruments.poll` records the word the app says TODAY, not the word T2b wants it to say. That is
deliberate and it is what makes the check at t2b.<loc> able to fire; a row holding the target would
be tautological. `instruments.convo` must be exactly "Convo" (T3) and is a HARD failure, never
routable to knownViolations — once a locale has a row it can no longer quietly stop saying Convo.
